steps.text: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl until well blended; set aside. Preheat a waffle iron to desired temperature.
Beat eggs in a separate bowl; stir in milk, melted butter, and vanilla until well combined.
Pour milk mixture into flour mixture; beat until blended.
Ladle batter into the preheated waffle iron.
Cook waffles until golden and crisp.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Waffles
raw_recipe.description: These crispy waffles are easy to make with simple ingredients you probably already have on hand for a light and fluffy breakfast treat or dessert.

video.description: These restaurant quality waffles are an easy-to-make breakfast! In this video, the Allrecipes team shows you how to make fluffy classic waffles using a homemade waffle batter. After mixing together the batter with flour, vanilla extract, sugar, and an egg mixture, pour the batter onto a waffle iron. Finally, cook the waffles until golden and crispy. With butter and a drizzle of maple syrup, these soft and delicious waffles are a picture-perfect morning meal.

review.reviewBody: We all enjoyed these for breakfast with sliced strawberries and whipped cream. The only thing I do differently is make waffles in the blender. First I whip up the egg in the blender then add the rest of the wet ingredients and blend quickly. Then add the mixed dry ingredients to the blender and use the stir cycle until well mixed. Then I pour it directly onto the waffle iron. I add extra milk to thin out the batter if it needs it. Easy! and a nice treat. Enjoy.

The only thing I did different than the directions stated to do was I sifted the flour, baking power & sugar before I added the liquid ingredients. If we could my husband and I would give this a 10 star rating. Also remember to put the hot waffle on paper towels because otherwise they do get steamy/soggy without. Thank you for the wonderful recipe.. no more mixes for us!! YUMMO (just like Rachel Ray says) ;-)

I've made this recipe twice now. Now never even eating anything but Eggos and hubby buying me a waffle maker for Christmas, the first time I made this recipe I following the directions exactly and they were good but they weren't "OMG these are amazing!" ... Which is why I gave this 4 stars.. Today I made this recipe again but this time I followed the suggestions in the reviews.. I used 4 tablespoons sugar, 1 tablespoon vanilla, 1/2 cup of butter (1 stick) just b/c it's easier than have a alittle bit of butter left over to put away in the fridge, and 1 3/4 cup milk to make it just alittle easier to pour. Today's batch was amazing!!! What a difference! Now it's a 5 star recipe! And everyone wanted more! Also... another tip.. The first time I made this I shifted the flour and I beat the egg whites and yolks separately to make fluffier waffles b/c that's all you see online about how to make fluffy waffles. But it was alot of work so today I didn't do any of that and they were the same texture/fluffiness, so don't waste your time doing those extra steps. ENJOY!!!
1st time cooking waffles and it came out great. I agree that separating the yolks and whites makes it better. Fantastic recipe.

Having never made a waffle until now, and having never even eaten one other than an Eggo, I have no basis to compare this recipe with any other. Having said that, all I know is hubby and I enjoyed our breakfast this morning! In comparing this recipe with other similar recipes, including the one included in the manual, this one called for twice the amount of salt, so I reduced it by half keeping all other ingredients and measurements the same, and beat the eggs well to lighten them up. The waffle was crispy on the outside, but tender on the inside, with good flavor. My only criticism, and certainly no fault of the recipe, is that my waffle maker anyway, cooks unevenly, with some parts of the waffle browning more than others. Maybe it just takes practice spreading the batter?
Glad to find this recipe as it is close to my mother's recipe that I lost. I separated the eggs and folded in the whites last. This is the way my mom's recipe was and it makes the waffles lighter.
The comments about too much salt were spot on. When I read the comments I assumed that they were using salted butter, I used unsalted butter and mine were still very salty.

Waffles freeze so easily, I doubled the recipe. My big change was using egg nog I needed to use up in place of most of the milk. It was a good choice. I also added extra sugar, and at least half teaspoon of nutmeg, use more if you’re a nutmeg fan. The waffles came out crispy on the outside, and soft and sweet inside. The eggnog gave the leavening agents some extra umph so they were nice and fluffy, but toasty brown. I used a whisk on my eggs then tempered them with the melted butter. Added the mixture to warmed eggnog/milk mixture. Mixed the wet into the dry. This recipe could easily be altered to your own taste :-)

Perfect! I used the waffle plates on my Breville sear & press and followed the directions for 210’C on the top plate and 180’C on the bottom for 3 1/2 minutes and they were absolutely perfect! I used lactose free milk and added one extra spoonful of sugar 🥰

This turned out so well! Fluffy, buttery and delicious. We made sure to temper the eggs with a little bit of the warm milk before adding all of it, just to avoid potentially scrambling them. We also made some homemade coconut vanilla whipped cream to go with the waffles and it was (to quote our three year old and five year old), “the BEST waffle [they’d] ever had!” Thank you!
Easy recipe. Made per the instructions. They were crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside, and they tasted like donuts or Churros without cinnamon. My family loved them.

Dude, this reminded me of when you wake up to a cat giving you a dead rat. I followed the instructions perfectly, but it turned out horribly; it was super salty, and I had to throw it out, thinking I made a mistake. I checked the recipe, only to realise I WAS CORRECT. The recipe told me to add 4 teaspoons of baking powder; that has to be a mistake, because I don't know anyone who'd enjoy this. So please just use a different recipe. Also, I'm pretty sure the 3,000+ 5-star reviews are just bot accounts
Wasn't sweet enough, didn't really have any flavor, I even added more than it said
It makes cooking so easier
I had to add a little more milk to get a smoother batter consistency. Next time I would reduce the salt. I followed the half recipe. They were nice a fluffy though.
Super consistent recipe, easy to do, easy to adjust the flavors to your preference. A great base waffle recipe.

I made this recipe and it was one of the better waffle recipes I’ve made (and I’ve made several). I did how ever, add more milk to it. It was pretty dry and barely wanted to pour, but as soon as I added a little more milk it was super easy to throw into the pan and cooked perfectly!

The waffles were incredible. A family favorite for sure! My kids absolutely loved them and we were able to make 10 circle waffles with this mix. The taste was incredible and a recipe that is worth trying. We will be making this again 100%!
added cinnamon and choco chips

Nope. Not for me. Thank you for sharing your recipe but my waffles came out virtually tasteless and were the consistency of white bread - turning soggy once the syrup and butter was on them. Not sure why the ratings for this recipe are love it or hate it but not something I’ll try a second time. I do look forward though to trying out more of your recipes. I’m sure there are some good ones in there!
